apr-calculator.assumptionNote: Assumes a fixed nominal rate, monthly payments and upfront fees deducted from the loan proceeds.
benefits: Reveals the true cost of borrowing, not just the advertised rate.
Lets you compare two loan offers with different fee structures fairly.
Shows exactly how much fees add to your cost over the loan's life.

faqs.a: APR stands for annual percentage rate. It is the yearly cost of borrowing expressed as a percentage, including both the interest rate and certain fees, so it reflects the true price of the loan better than the nominal rate alone.

The nominal (stated) rate is the rate used to compute your monthly payment on the full loan amount. The APR is higher whenever there are upfront fees, because you effectively pay interest on money you never received. With no fees, the two are equal.
faqs.q: How is APR different from the interest rate?

faqs.a: Compare APRs for loans with the same term, because a longer term can make the APR look lower while total interest is higher. Also check for fees not included in the APR, such as late-payment charges.
faqs.q: How should I compare loan offers?

faqs.a: No. In many countries lenders must disclose APR, but the exact fee set included varies by regulation. Always read the loan disclosure to see which fees are inside the APR figure.

An APR is designed for installment loans with a fixed term. For revolving credit like credit cards, the effective rate depends on how you use and repay the balance, so a single APR number is less meaningful.
faqs.q: Can APR compare credit cards too?

faqs.a: This calculator solves the standard present-value equation numerically with a bisection search, which is the same definition regulators use: the discount rate that makes the present value of all payments equal to the amount you actually receive.

apr-calculator.formula:
monthly_payment = P x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n), r = nominal_rate / 12
APR = the rate r* that solves: net_received = payment x (1 - (1 + r*)^-n) / r*
APR_annual = r* x 12 (solved numerically)
howTo: Enter the loan amount before fees.
Enter the upfront fees charged by the lender.
Enter the nominal (advertised) annual interest rate.
Enter the loan term in years.
Read the true APR, your monthly payment and the total cost of fees plus interest.
keyFacts: APR, the annual percentage rate, expresses the total yearly cost of a loan as a single percentage.
It folds upfront fees and charges into the rate, so loans with the same nominal rate can have different APRs.
A $10,000 loan at 8% with $200 in fees over 3 years has a true APR of about 9.38%, not 8%.
Comparing APRs is the fairest way to compare loan offers with different fee structures.
Regulators in many countries require lenders to disclose APR so borrowers can compare offers.
